1. The present appeals are filed by the original claimants under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as the "Act, 1988") being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award dated 30/03/2013 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal Rajeshbhai Rayjibhai Mahera vs Dabhi Bharatsinh Kishorsinh on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10013950/
1 (Auxiliary) and Additional District Judge, Kheda at Nadiad in MACP No.2686 of 2003 and MACP No.2687 of 2003.

2. Short facts of the claim case are as under:
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/339/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined 2.1.

On 23/08/2003 at about 5:00 p.m. near Namnar Village patia on Daver to Angervada road, the claimants of both the claim petitions and other went in Jeep bearing registration no.GJ-10-E-2027 but as there was puncture in it, it was parked on the road side and when the driver was changing the wheel, the applicants-claimants stood behind that jeep and at that time the opponent no.1 came with a Loading Tempo bearing registration no.GJ-17-X-7387 at a high speed in rash and negligent manner endangering to human life and dashed on the back side of that Jeep.
As a result of the same the said Tempo ran over both the legs of the applicants-claimants and thereby the accident took place which caused serious injures and fracture to the applicants-claimants.
For the same, an FIR was lodged bearing I-C.R. No.75 of 2003 before the Kothamba Police Station.

2.2. The present appellants-original claimants therefore filed claim petitions being Motor Accident Claim Petition No.2686 of 2003 and Motor Accident Claim Petition No.2687 of 2003 under the provisions of Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.4,00,000/- in MACP No.2686 of 2003 and Rs.2,00,000/- in MACP No.2687 against the respondents.

sentences.text:
2.3. Vide the aforesaid impugned judgment and award, the learned Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petitions preferred by the appellants-original claimants under Section 166 of the Act, 1988 holding that the appellants-original NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/339/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined claimants are entitle to receive compensation of an amount of Rs.57,000/- in MACP No.2686 of 2003 and Rs.53,200/- in MACP No.2687 of 2003 with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of such claim petitions till its actual realization.
3.

This Court vide order dated 24/02/2014, noticing the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellants- original claimants and the grounds raised in the present appeals, has admitted the appeals.

4. The learned counsel for the appellants-original claimants has submitted that the learned Tribunal has committed an error in awarding inadequate compensation to the claimants and has failed to appreciate the evidence on record in its true perspective.

It is also submitted that the learned Tribunal has not properly assessed the income of the appellants-original claimants and has overlooked the settled principles of law in relation to the assessment of other conventional heads like future loss of income, pain, shock and suffering, loss of amenities of life, medical expenses,
transportation charges etc. 4.1.

It is also submitted by learned counsel for the appellants-claimants that the learned Tribunal has erred in decreasing percentage of disability of the claimant from 44%
Rajeshbhai Rayjibhai Mahera vs Dabhi Bharatsinh Kishorsinh on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10013950/
2 to 30% in MACP No.2686 of 2003 and decreasing percentage of disability of the claimant from 34%
to 23% in MACP No.2687 of 2003 without giving any findings on that aspect.

entities.text: Rajeshbhai Rayjibhai Mahera vs Dabhi Bharatsinh Kishorsinh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/339/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined is also submitted that the learned Tribunal has erred in considering 50% negligence on part of the party of the Jeep.

The learned counsel has therefore urged that the impugned judgment and award of the learned Tribunal is not just, fair, and reasonable and it is required to be modified as per the settled legal principles.

5. Learned counsels appearing for the respective respondents have placed reliance upon the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal and submitted that the compensation must be awarded as just,
proper and reasonable.

They have further submitted that the learned Tribunal, after appreciating the material available on record, awarded the compensation under each head which is just, proper and reasonable and not required to be interfered in these appeals and lastly prayed to dismiss the present appeals.
6.

Heard learned counsels appearing for the respective parties and perused the documents on record and the impugned judgment and award, more particularly, the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal while considering the issue of quantum of compensation as well as the issue of negligence.

7. With regard to the submission on the point of disability in MACP No.2686 of 2003, in the impugned judgment and award, more particularly in para-16, what the Tribunal has observed is just and proper and the same is not required to be NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/339/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined interfered.

In para-16, the Tribunal has observed as under:
"16.

Moreover, in order to prove disability, the applicant has produced disability certificate at Exh.23 issued by Dr. Yogesh Parikh of Tulsi Hospital, Nadiad, who has assessed the permanent disability of 44% in relation to whole body.
In order to prove the same, the applicant has examined the said doctor before this Tribunal at Exh.22,

but in his cross-examination made by the ld. advocate for the opponent no.3, this medical expert has admitted that he had not examined any proof about age of patient Baberbhai, he admitted that he had not given any treatment, not seen any report of x-ray or radiologist, he further admitted that there can be some reduction in disability up to 2-3 percent of body as a whole if treatment of physiotherapy is taken

,
lastly he admitted that he had not assessed the functional disability of patient.

In view of above discussion, and considering the cross-examination of Dr.Yogesh Parikh, this Tribunal is of the view that the permanent disability of applicant should be assessed at 30% body as a whole."
7.1.

Similarly, with regard to the submission on the point of disability in MACP No.2687 of 2003, in the impugned judgment and award, more particularly in para-16 with regard to MACP No.2687 of 2003, what the Tribunal has observed is just and proper and the same is not required to be interfered.

In para-16 with regard to MACP No.2687 of 2003, the Tribunal has observed as under:
"16.

Moreover, in order to prove disability, the applicant has produced disability certificate at Exh.20 issued by Dr. Yogesh Parikh of Tulsi Hospital, Nadiad, who has Rajeshbhai Rayjibhai Mahera vs Dabhi Bharatsinh Kishorsinh on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10013950/
3 assessed the permanent disability of 34% in relation to whole body.

In order to prove the same, the applicant has examined the said doctor before this Tribunal at Exh.19,
but in his cross-examination made by the ld.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/339/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/08/2025

undefined advocate for the opponent no.3, this medical expert has admitted that he had not examined any proof about age of patient Rajeshbhai, he admitted that he had not given any treatment, not seen any report of x-ray or radiologist, he further admitted that there can be some reduction in disability, if treatment of physiotherapy is taken, lastly he admitted that he had not assessed the functional disability of patient.

In view of above discussion, and considering the cross-examination of Dr.Yogesh Parikh, this Tribunal is of the view that the permanent disability of applicant should be assessed at 23% body as a whole."
8.

In para-19 of the impugned judgment and award, after computing award, the Tribunal has observed for MACP No.2686 of 2003 as under:
"19. ..... the applicant has not jointed the driver, owner and Ins. Co. of jeep no.GJ-10E-2027, he is not entitled to get 50% of total amount i.e. Rs.57,000/- and hence he is only awarded Rs.57,000/-.

So, I award the same to the applicant in the claim petition no.2686/03."
8.1.

Similarly, in para-19 of the impugned judgment and award, after computing award, the Tribunal has observed for MACP No.2687 of 2003 as under:
"19. ..... the applicant has not jointed the driver, owner and Ins. Co. of jeep no.GJ-10E-2027, he is not entitled to get 50% of total amount i.e. Rs.53,200/- and hence he is only awarded Rs.53,220/-, which is rounded up to Rs,53,200/-.
So, I award the same to the applicant in the claim petition no.2687/03."

9. In the judgment of Khenyei Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., reported in (2015) 9 SCC 273, it is observed as under:
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/339/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined "22.

entities.text: Khenyei Vs. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., reported in (2015) 9 SCC 273
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
What emerges from the aforesaid discussion is as follows :
22.1

In the case of composite negligence, plaintiff/claimant is entitled to sue both or any one of the joint tort feasors and to recover the entire compensation as liability of joint tort feasors is joint and several.
22.2 In the case of composite negligence, apportionment of compensation between two tort feasors vis-a-vis the plaintiff/claimant is not permissible.
He can recover at his option whole damages from any of them.
Rajeshbhai Rayjibhai Mahera vs Dabhi Bharatsinh Kishorsinh on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10013950/

entities.text: Rajeshbhai Rayjibhai Mahera vs Dabhi Bharatsinh Kishorsinh on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In case all the joint tort feasors have been impleaded and evidence is sufficient,
it is open to the court/tribunal to determine inter se extent of composite negligence of the drivers.

However, determination of the extent of negligence between the joint tort feasors is only for the purpose of their inter se liability so that one may recover the sum from the other after making whole of payment to the plaintiff/claimant to the extent it has satisfied the liability of the other.

In case both of them have been impleaded and the apportionment/ extent of their negligence has been determined by the court/tribunal, in main case one joint tort feasor can recover the amount from the other in the execution proceedings.
22.4 It would not be appropriate for the court/tribunal to determine the extent of composite negligence of the drivers of two vehicles in the absence of impleadment of other joint tort feasors.

In such a case, impleaded joint tort feasor should be left, in case he so desires, to sue the other joint NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/339/2014 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/08/2025 undefined tort feasor in independent proceedings after passing of the decree or award."
10.

In view of above cited decision, the observation of the Tribunal with regard to liability is not just,
proper and reasonable and the same is required to be interfered by this Court in these appeals.
Accordingly, the claimants are entitled to recover total amount of compensation from the present respondents.
11. So far as compensation awarded under the other heads are concerned, the Tribunal has awarded just and proper compensation under each head and hence the same requires no interference.

12. For the foregoing reasons, the impugned judgment and award dated 30/03/2013 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Auxiliary) and Additional District Judge, Kheda at Nadiad in MACP No.2686 of 2003 and MACP No.2687 of 2003 is hereby modified.

The respondent nos.1 to 3 are liable to pay the same jointly and severally together with interest at the rate of 7.5% from the date of filing of the claim petitions till realization.

Let, the aforesaid amount be deposited with the concerned Tribunal within a period of 8 weeks from the date of receipt of the present order.

On deposit of the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall be at liberty to release and disburse the entire award amount in favour of the respective original claimants, after due verification as per the original judgment and award.

15. 5 from deposit of such amount.
